purpose: A labelled corpus for the matched-condition harness (GOAL F1). Each `signature` is a past failure the store has learned; each `episode` is a trajectory the agent is on. A positive episode names the signature that SHOULD be surfaced; a negative episode names none and must stay silent.
provenance: Every signature is a failure this project actually had, taken from CHANGELOG.md, the audit rounds and the loop ledger. The episodes are hand-written paraphrases of the situation immediately BEFORE each failure - deliberately not the wording of the note, because an episode that quotes its own note measures string matching and reports it as anticipation.
limitations: n is small and single-author. It supports a precision/recall CURVE and a matched-FPR comparison; it does not support a population estimate.

The paraphrases are written by the same author as the notes. That biases toward recall - a real user's phrasing would share fewer content words. The negatives are the guard against reading too much into that: they are drawn from ordinary work in the same repository and vocabulary.
Ground truth is single-label top-1. An episode heading toward two past failures at once is not represented.

signatures.title: test code wrote to the owner's real memory store
signatures.text: test or example code resolved the vault to the owner's live Obsidian memory store and wrote into it, clobbering real notes

signatures.title: training ran on cpu because device was never set
signatures.text: the model was left on cpu instead of cuda so training throughput silently collapsed to a fraction of the gpu speed

signatures.title: embedding cache built by one model queried by another
signatures.text: the embedding cache was written by one embedder and then queried with vectors from a different model, so cosine similarity returned meaningless neighbours

signatures.title: generator died on import while its wrapper logged success
signatures.text: the graph generator raised on import and the wrapper caught the exception and logged success anyway, so the artifact was stale for a month with nothing reporting it

signatures.title: concurrent writers raced on one temporary file
signatures.text: several threads inside one process wrote the same state file through a temp name that carried only the pid, so the rename failed with a sharing violation on windows and silently lost a writer on posix

signatures.title: unbounded recurrence count from a note file
signatures.text: a recurrence count read straight from note frontmatter was never bounded, so one hand-edited note claiming an enormous count outranked every other memory forever

signatures.title: a published number outlived the code that produced it
signatures.text: a benchmark figure stayed in the documentation after the code that produced it changed, so the published number described a tree that no longer existed

signatures.title: verification ran before the new files were staged
signatures.text: the test suite was run before the new files were added to git, so every git-driven check could not see them and passed while continuous integration went red

signatures.title: two verification runs shared one working tree
signatures.text: a mutation harness and a full test run were started at the same time in the same directory, so each saw the other's edits and the results were meaningless

signatures.title: the mutation changed the checker instead of the artifact
signatures.text: the mutation weakened the validating code rather than the document being validated, so the suite stayed green and the guarantee was never actually tested

signatures.title: a one-shot timing was published as a cost
signatures.text: a latency figure came from a single run whose value moved substantially between sessions, and it was published as though it were a stable measurement

signatures.title: shell heredoc mangled a regex escape
signatures.text: a patch applied through a shell heredoc turned a backslash escape into a literal control character, producing code that failed while printing the string it expected

signatures.title: a credential reached the store before redaction
signatures.text: an api key pasted into a transcript was written into a note on disk because redaction ran on the display path and not on the write path

signatures.title: a truncated write destroyed the live file
signatures.text: a file was opened for writing and the process failed partway through, leaving the previously good contents replaced by an empty or half-written file

signatures.title: a guard promoted and demoted forever
signatures.text: demotion cleared only the supporting sessions and not the opposing ones, so the next report promoted the guard again and it could never retire
